title: Unverified: AP Promise-Tracking Criteria and Trump’s Delivery Narrative
description_short: AP tracks selected Trump promises; the supplied criticism of its criteria remains unverified.
description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Donald Trump’s promise-delivery messaging shifted while the criteria used to judge completion remained unclear. AP’s tracker page says it follows selected 2024 campaign promises and presents a status and method for each. That page verifies the tracker’s scope, not the entry’s criticism of shifting rhetoric, ambiguous criteria, or resulting accountability costs. Keep those claims unpublished pending a named pledge and dated evidence.
description_long: The supplied record alleges that Trump’s campaign-promise delivery narrative relied on forceful messaging while leaving the standards for judging completion unclear. The Associated Press page linked in the packet identifies a project tracking selected promises from Trump’s 2024 campaign; it lists each promise with a status and a method, and says it was last updated on December 3, 2025. This confirms the tracker’s existence and stated format, but it does not establish that Trump changed his account, that AP’s standards shifted, or that any specific promise was assessed under ambiguous criteria. The packet names no pledge, dated status change, evaluation rule, or before-and-after statement that could support those allegations. The claimed accountability costs are also not tied to a documented outcome. This draft preserves the original criticism as an unverified claim for internal review, not as an AP finding. The frozen March 4, 2026 date remains supplied and unverified; the cited page’s December 2025 update is project context and does not establish a separate March event. A named pledge and dated evidence linking a changed account or criterion to it are still needed.

title: Unverified Allegation: August 2025 Pardons Favored Allies and White-Collar Defendants
description_short: The supplied record alleges an August 2025 pardon wave favoring allies; its date, recipients, donor links, and process remain unverified.
description_medium: The supplied record alleges that Trump issued an August 2025 wave of pardons favoring white-collar defendants and political allies, with donor connections and reduced DOJ review. The prior research notes say they did not verify a distinct August 22 pardon wave or a donor link. This internal draft attributes those claims to the supplied record and does not state that the pardons occurred as described.
description_long: The supplied record alleges that Donald Trump issued a wave of pardons in August 2025 benefiting wealthy white-collar defendants and political allies, including people who had refused to cooperate with investigators. It further alleges that the grants bypassed normal Department of Justice review and favored people who had made substantial contributions to Trump’s political committees. These remain allegations supplied for drafting; this card does not present them as established events or findings. The prior research note states that it could not verify a discrete August 22 pardon wave matching the claim or evidence that the recipients were major Trump donors. No recipient names, pardon warrants, dated list of grants, donor matches, or review records are supplied here. A DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney page listing clemency grants was located as a research reference, but the accessed search result did not establish the claimed August 22 group or the asserted financial relationships. Without records tying identified recipients to the same date and donor claim, the date, scale, motives, process, and beneficiary descriptions remain unresolved. Keep this draft unpublished until source material supports those specific allegations.

title: Unverified Allegation: Hegseth Made Trump Loyalty a Promotion Requirement
description_short: The supplied claim of a Trump-loyalty test for military promotions is unverified and conflicts with cited merit-based policy language.
description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Hegseth changed military promotion rules in March 2025 to require loyalty to Trump. The prior notes say no directive establishing that test was found and cite DoD language describing promotion decisions as merit-based. A March 7 Hill opinion criticized a senior appointment as signaling loyalty over competence, but it does not establish a formal promotion rule. This internal draft remains unpublished.
description_long: The supplied entry alleges that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth restructured military promotions in March 2025 so that loyalty to Donald Trump would outweigh merit and professional qualifications. The supplied research notes state that no credible directive or report was located establishing an explicit Trump-loyalty test. Those notes cite Department of Defense materials describing promotion and selection decisions as merit-based and a later review memorandum calling for fair, transparent, objective procedures; the cited government pages returned HTTP 403 in this run, so those descriptions remain supplied research context rather than newly accessed quotations. Exa search did return a March 7, 2025 Hill opinion passage arguing that the selection of retired Lt. Gen. Dan Caine could signal political loyalty over competency-based advancement. That commentary concerns one senior appointment and expresses an opinion; it does not establish a change to the military promotion system. Reports of senior-officer or military-lawyer removals likewise would not prove such a rule. This draft therefore preserves the original allegation only for internal review. It does not state that a loyalty test was enacted or that predicted effects on readiness occurred. The exact blocker is a missing directive, promotion instruction, or credible report documenting the alleged March rule and its scope.

title: Unverified Allegation: Trump Administration Dismantled Federal Prison Rehabilitation Programs
description_short: The supplied March 2025 claim of wholesale First Step Act program dismantling is unverified; a later BOP directive called for implementation.
description_medium: The supplied record alleges that the administration dismantled First Step Act rehabilitation programs in March 2025. The packet identifies no March directive ending education, treatment, vocational training, and reentry programs. A June 17 BOP release instead announced a directive for robust First Step Act and Second Chance Act implementation. That later action does not rule out specific earlier disruptions, so the original claim remains an unpublished allegation.
description_long: The supplied record alleges that in March 2025 the Trump administration dismantled First Step Act implementation by ending federal prison education, vocational training, substance-use treatment, and reentry programs, eliminating related funding, and abolishing educator, counselor, and social-worker positions. The packet’s prior research notes say no March directive ending all non-security rehabilitation programming was found. It also identifies a Bureau of Prisons release dated June 17, 2025, announcing a policy memorandum directing robust and comprehensive implementation of both the First Step Act and the Second Chance Act. That later announcement is important contrary context, but it does not by itself disprove a particular March cut, temporary interruption, staffing action, or facility-level change. The supplied material does not identify a March order, affected facilities, positions, program names, budget records, or implementation data supporting the sweeping claim. This internal draft preserves the allegation without presenting wholesale dismantling as an established fact. It does not add the separate mandatory-sentencing claim as proof of rehabilitation-program cuts. The exact blocker is contemporaneous documentation identifying what changed in March, where it changed, and whether the claimed programs or positions were actually ended. The original March 1 date remains approximate and unverified.
